rules.statement: For one key, installs happen in the order loads started (P6).

Snapshot caches have ttl = null and throw on failed reads, whoever creates them (a snapshot cache built outside the starter is pinned all the same), and no customizer replaces a CoSec cache's codec, loaders, key filter or per-entry lifetime; an instance refuses to start when Redis's maxmemory-policy is not noeviction.

rules.statement: Once the platform's limits or attributes change, every app and tenant document installed afterwards was compiled with them or is compiled again, including one whose load was in flight; one that cannot be compiled again fails closed.
guards: runtime:SnapshotRecompileTest#a load that compiled with the old inputs while they changed is compiled again before anyone is served it

rules.statement: A tenant configured to fail closed on lag (`cosec.authorization.snapshot.fail-closed.tenants`) is not decided on when the oldest document its evaluation reads was last confirmed by the store longer ago than `fail-closed.max-lag`: the request is indeterminate (503) unless a DENY matches. Other tenants, and views within the bound, are decided as usual.
guards: runtime:DocumentSnapshotViewsTest#a fail-closed tenant past its lag bound is unresolved, others decide

rules.statement: The periodic revalidation cannot be turned off or left unbounded: `cosec.authorization.snapshot.revalidate-interval` is at least 1 second, at most 5 minutes, less than `lag-warn` and, with fail-closed tenants, less than `fail-closed.max-lag`, or startup fails naming it. Installed documents are revalidated by periodic passes, each a conditional read of the store per document, never a local copy, and a reset of the change channel reloads them all. A pass starts every interval or, when the previous one is still in flight, as soon as it ends; a change whose invalidation was lost, or whose reload failed, is installed by the first pass that reaches its document after the change is readable. A pass that has finished no document for `storeReadTimeout` and has no read in flight is abandoned at the next tick; a pass with a read in flight never is.
guards: spring-boot:CoSecPipelineAutoConfigurationTest#a revalidate-interval that turns off or unbinds the periodic pass fails startup

rules.statement: An entry for a document the store does not hold never evicts one it holds: such entries have a bound of their own (`maxAbsent` per family) and evict only each other, so however many ids without a document a client names, every document a family holds within its bound stays installed.
guards: runtime:DocumentSnapshotSourceTest#a flood of ids without a document never evicts a document

rules.statement: A revision whose compilation fails, with an exception or a VirtualMachineError such as a StackOverflowError, is installed as failed: the source never keeps serving the revision before it in its place.
guards: runtime:SnapshotSourceFailureTest#f5NewRevisionWhoseCompilationOverflowsTheStackReplacesTheInstalledOne
runtime:SnapshotReviewFixesTest#virtualMachineErrorInACompilationFailsTheLoadWithoutWedgingTheKey

rules.statement: Every key a deployment writes to Redis lives under its one `cosec.key-prefix`: snapshot documents, control-plane records, candidates, shadow reports, revocations, memberships, API keys, rate limit counters and OAuth states. Two deployments on one Redis that differ in it share no key. An environment that sets one of the three prefixes it replaced fails startup whatever `cosec.unknown-properties` says, naming the families that move and that revocations and API keys must be copied first, so no revocation is left where nothing reads it.
guards: spring-boot:DeploymentKeyPrefixTest#every key family the starter wires lives under cosec key-prefix
